title: Model choice heuristics and sales scripts
content:
Purpose / summary:

This doc is an internal GTM play we can use to help field teams (AEs, SEs, solutions) quickly explain how Redwood’s model catalog and verified profiles reduce risk, speed time-to-value, and make model selection repeatable for production inference. Focus is on simple heuristics, a 90-second sales script, a short objection playbook, and two one-page decision aids for customers (developer persona + product persona).

Audience:
- AEs and SEs prepping for calls with engineering/product leads
- Solutions engineers running POCs
- Content & demand teams who need concise messaging and example talk tracks

Core positioning lines to memorize (one-liners):
- "Redwood gives you curated model options with transparent performance and cost trade-offs so you don’t have to invent model ops from scratch."
- "Verified profiles mean we’ve run the models against realistic inference workloads — we publish latency, cost-per-1000-tokens, and quality baselines so you can choose by objective, not buzz."
- "If latency, cost, and regulatory controls each pull you in different directions, our catalog helps you pick the right variant and routing policy without guesswork."

90-second demo/sales script (bullet flow for reps):
1) Intro (15s): "We’re Redwood Inference — we help teams run LLMs at predictable cost and latency across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
2) Problem (15s): "Choosing a model for production is noisy: benchmarks are inconsistent, quantized variants change behavior, and infra trade-offs are hidden until you scale."
3) Solution (30s): "Our model catalog offers open model variants plus Redwood-verified profiles — each profile shows measured latency, token cost, sample outputs on common evals, and recommended quant/serving configs. We also provide routing and fallback rules so you can prioritize SLOs or unit cost in production."
4) Proof point (15s): "On our typical ecommerce workload, switching to a recommended 8-bit variant plus prefix caching cut per-token cost by 43% with negligible quality regression — we publish those measurements in the profile."
5) CTA (15s): "If you have a target latency and quality bar, we can run a guided POC: pick two candidate profiles, run your sample prompt set, and compare cost/latency/quality in a shared dashboard in under two weeks."

Model choice heuristics (short checklist SEs/AEs can use live):
- Start with the objective: is this primarily latency-bound, cost-bound, or quality-bound?
- For latency-bound (user-facing prompts, <300ms SLO): pick smaller verified families and single-region routing; enable KV/prefix cache and continuous batching that favors low tail latency.
- For cost-bound (high throughput asynchronous embeddings or offline generation): pick quantized variants with batch-optimized kernels and enable larger batch sizes + burst capacity.
- For quality-bound (safety checks, summarization, legal): pick higher-capacity variants and choose profiles with explicit evals on long context and factuality tests.
- Always review the verified profile’s sample outputs on your domain prompts; if outputs drift, flag as potential fine-tune or retrieval need.

What’s in a verified profile (how we sell it):
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for typical token lengths and sequence distributions
- Unit cost estimate (tokens/sec, $/1k tokens) for hosted and dedicated configs
- Model variants (float16, 8-bit, 4-bit) and recommended hardware classes
- Quality snapshot: selected eval scores (summarization ROUGE/BLEU-like proxies where relevant) and curated example prompts including failure modes
- Serving knobs: batching suggestions, caching strategy, and routing fallbacks
- Known incompatibilities (e.g., inconsistent tool-calling behavior post-quantization)

Objection playbook (short):
- "We can’t risk regression if we change model variants." -> "We run side-by-side evals on your prompt set and will only enable a quantized/cheaper variant if regressions are within agreed thresholds; rollback is automated and instant."
- "We need on-prem/VPC only." -> "Profiles include recommended Dedicated/Private configs with KMS/HSM and audit logs; the measured latencies include private environment baselines."
- "Benchmarks are synthetic and won’t match our workload." -> "We’ll replicate a small sample of your traffic and publish the profile against that real workload — that is part of the POC deliverable."

Two one-page decision aids (copyable to slides):
1) Developer checklist (for hands-on engineers):
- Define SLOs (p50 latency, p95 latency, throughput targets)
- Collect 50–200 representative prompts or embedding queries
- Pick two profile candidates (one quality-first, one cost-first)
- Run 1-week smoke test with A/B traffic split and inspect sample outputs + error traces
- If drift observed -> add retrieval or narrow prompt engineering before changing model family

2) Product/PM checklist (for business stakeholders):
- What user experience depends on latency vs. accuracy?
- What is acceptable cost per MAU or per query?
- Which data residency/compliance controls are required?
- Acceptable time-to-fix for safety regressions (SLA)
- Rollout plan: canary -> ramp -> auto-fallback triggers

Competitive talking points (short differentiation bullets):
- Against general-purpose cloud model endpoints: "We publish workload-aware profiles and suggest concrete serving configs — not just raw model access."
- Against one-off benchmarking vendors: "We link benchmarks to operational serving knobs and rollout automation, so verified performance translates to production economics."
- Against closed-model incumbents: "You can start with open-model variants we’ve verified and fall back to higher-capacity options; the catalog prioritizes repeatability and observability rather than opaque model claims."

Examples / micro-case study to cite on calls (brief):
- Retail search re-rank POC: Customer had 7s re-rank latency at scale on a CPU-hosted pipeline. Redwood recommended an 8-bit variant and KV cache for stable prefixes; measured p95 dropped to 420ms and unit cost fell 38% in Dedicated mode. (internal ID: GT-REB-2025-09)

Open questions / follow-ups (for product/content):
- Can we add a lightweight "customer sample-run" checkbox in the profile so SEs can request a shared POC snapshot? (prio: high)
- Need a templated HTML one-pager per profile that contains sample outputs and an interactive latency/cost slider for the docs site. (owner: Product content)

Quick assets to attach to the play:
- 1-slide cheat sheet for AEs (90s script + 3 bullets)
- Email cadence template for initiating a model-profile POC
- A short Loom showing how to read a verified profile in the console

Sample outreach email (for AEs to start a POC):
Subject: Quick POC to compare two model profiles for <customer-product>
Hi <Name>,
We’ve helped teams like <customer-ref> cut inference cost while keeping quality stable by validating model profiles against real prompts. Want to run a short 2-week POC where we compare a quality-first and a cost-first profile on 100 of your real queries? We’ll deliver a side-by-side dashboard with latency, cost estimates, and sample outputs. If that sounds useful I’ll route in an SE and a short kickoff.

Notes to self (work-in-progress):
- Keep this doc intentionally simple — majority of field use will be copy-paste from the AE cheat sheet.
- Coordinate with product to ensure the profile JSON fields align with any newly shipped console metrics (p99 tokens/sec, cold-start penalty).
- Add one-line competitor rebuttals to shared content before next enablement session.
